Fortitude

/FOR-tih-tood/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Fortitude means strength of mind in facing danger, pain, or adversity; courage under strain.

Fortitude means strength of mind in facing danger, pain, or adversity; courage under strain. It took real fortitude for the rookie reporter to keep asking questions while the crowd jeered.

Worked Example

The polar research station lost its generator in the third week of the winter dark. While the crew waited for parts that could not arrive for a month, the temperature indoors fell below freezing. The station chief rationed fuel, kept the team on schedule, and never once let panic into her voice. Crew members later said her steadiness was the only thing that kept the outpost together. Reports credited the rescue less to luck than to her extraordinary fortitude.

The chief's unshaken steadiness of mind through a month of cold, darkness, and danger — holding the crew together without panic — is what fortitude means.

How Fortitude Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

endurance

endurance: the power to keep going through strain

grit

grit: toughness of spirit

Antonyms

cowardice

cowardice: lack of courage

faintheartedness

faintheartedness: timidity in the face of difficulty

How Strong Is It? — patience → fortitude → heroism

patience vs. fortitude

patience vs. fortitude: Patience is the milder quality — quietly waiting things out; fortitude adds real courage, holding steady against danger, pain, or fear.

heroism vs. fortitude

heroism vs. fortitude: Heroism is stronger than fortitude: it goes beyond enduring hardship bravely to taking extraordinary action at great personal risk.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — fort

Root — fort: strong (Latin fortis)

Suffix — -itude

Suffix — -itude: noun-forming: state or quality of

Put it together

Put it together: Fortitude comes straight from Latin fortitudo, 'strength,' built on fortis (strong) plus the quality-suffix -itude. English kept the root busy: fortify (make strong), fortress (a strong place), effort (strength exerted). Fortitude is the inner version — a fortress of the mind that holds while everything outside it shakes.

Use the root in a new word: fortress

Use the root in a new word: fortress: The hilltop fortress withstood every siege for a century — fortress comes from the same Latin fortis (strong) that gives a person of fortitude their inner stronghold.
